summary.name: 3D Motion Graphics (Digital and 3D Aesthetics, supplemental provenance). A user-requested broad direction. It does not require photorealism or one specific rendering engine.
summary.visualIdentity: Genuine 3D geometry in a rendering style chosen before modeling: photorealistic, cartoon, or stylized. Requires coherent bevels, roughness, reflections, contact shadows, and a clear key light. Perspective or orthographic framing is chosen deliberately.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to hero renders where the object is the message. Explicit combinations name product launch films, brand stings, and hardware feature breakdowns. Other fits are inferred from catalog compatibility, such as product motion, dioramas, and exploded views.
summary.limitations: Flat image scaling is not a 3D dolly, and a single flat sprite cannot show unseen sides. Text should not be rendered inside 3D geometry. Soft shadows alone do not establish photorealism. Avoid intersections, floating objects, inconsistent scale, and blown-out highlights. Basic XPBD does not provide fluid, plastic, origami, or rigid-body contact behavior without added models.
summary.palette: The palette is an optional, reference-dependent example, not an intrinsic style palette. Suggested tokens: background #EDE9E1, foreground #303C40, accent_1 #748E8A, accent_2 #B9866C. Task, brand, or reference colors override them. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 9.395:1, while accent fills reach only 3.239 and 3.624 for body text, so they are decorative only. Two-color checks do not verify text over video or texture.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Video motion derives from composition time, and interactive delivery may add pointer, scroll, or click input. Weighted rotation, assembly, and camera moves should keep deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds. Motion references are optional and need matching scene geometry. Explicit examples include a drop-and-growth trigger, a helix camera journey, a full orbit, and a radial logo burst.
summary.audio: Unspecified in the source; no audio layer is mandated. Options include restrained accents, ambience, music, voiceover, or silence, chosen from the topic. Honor explicit user audio first and do not invent audio assets. Beat or music synchronization requires actual audio analysis. Speech intelligibility and picture sync must be verified.
summary.assetRequirements: Authorized 3D models or glTF assets are required, with node names, pivots, materials, and dimensions inspected after loading. Embedded animation clips must be confirmed, not inferred from filenames. Normal and roughness maps are non-color data. Screen footage must be authorized, and fonts and assets must load before rendering. Orbit references need complete geometry or enough turntable views.
summary.combinations: Explicit pairings: style-093 adds 2D kinetic titles over Blender shots, with titles sharing the camera easing and never intersecting geometry. style-109 adds 2D leader-line callouts anchored to exported 3D positions, drawn only when the object is at rest. Avoid text inside 3D and fast type cuts against slow camera moves.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: Blender with Python bpy and Cycles or EEVEE, or the listed Three.js PBR alternative. Motion engine: bpy keyframes, optional XPBD with a verified solver, glTF part animation, or raycast camera control. HyperFrames is the default pipeline, with Remotion only as a recorded fallback. Bake simulations before rendering frame sequences.
